artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of a whole Missal, 123,278 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes. It is registered as a source artifact and nothing more, and it is deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records; the prior lt-hist corpus cut the same text into twelve markdown 'sections' bounded by line ranges over the downloaded file, and reproducing that shape here would reproduce a defect with better provenance attached.

WHY ROUTE (a) WAS NOT TAKEN, AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE. The pattern this repository uses when a tracked text carries matter its basis does not cover is a single stated replayable transformation -- `sed '140854,141805d' SOURCE > OUT` on the Lasance artifact, one contiguous appendix on printed-page boundaries, no program, no judgement. That pattern does not fit this book, and the reason is structural rather than laborious. The post-1920 matter is in at least five different parts of the book at once: eight day-entries interleaved through the kalendarium table at 5372, 6195, 6378, 7284, 7388, 7420, 7856 and 8133; a Praefatio indexed at 43750, 43801 and 46562; occurrence and transfer rubrics at 11241 and 48595-48607; nine sanctoral or temporal formularies at 66667, 72586, 74820, 86104, 86897, 87420, 87798, 92091 and 94367; and the appendix Mass at 120199-120390. AND SOME OF IT IS NOT ADDITIVE AT ALL, WHICH IS WHAT KILLS THE ROUTE RATHER THAN MERELY BURDENING IT. Two of the nine are REPLACEMENTS. The Mass Signum magnum of 1950 displaced the older Assumption formulary, so deleting it leaves 15 August with no Mass at all rather than with the one the 1920 typical edition printed. The Immaculate Heart took 22 August from Ss. Timothy, Hippolytus and Symphorian, who survive in this book only as the commemoration attached to it at kalendarium 7421, and its own rubric at 87803-87804 then suppresses what would otherwise be said of the Assumption octave on that day -- so deleting the 1944 entry leaves 22 August holding a commemoration with no feast to hang on. A deletion cannot restore a displaced text; it can only remove the thing that displaced it and leave the hole. AND THE LIST COULD NOT BE PROVED COMPLETE. There is no copy of the 1920 typical edition in this repository to diff against; the tracked 1570 and 1604 witness the ancient stratum but not what Divino afflatu changed in 1920. A hand-picked deletion list with no control, presented as exhaustive, is the undisclosed editorial hand that src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml `[[corrections]]` `the-google-scans-carry-a-stamp-and-not-the-boilerplate` refused in its own words, with the added defect that nobody could check it.

WHAT MAY STILL BE QUOTED, STATED POSITIVELY BECAUSE A RIGHTS RECORD LANDED ON 2026-08-01 DEPENDS ON IT. Everything this repository has so far read out of these bytes is preexisting material of the 1920 typical edition or older, and 17 U.S.C. 103(b) leaves it exactly where it was. Named, with the loci: the Canon Missae at 49251; the Corpus Christi propers at 56316-56590, cited from src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml; the All Souls formularies at 95538-96280, cited from the same file; the Ordo Missae, the Ritus servandus and De defectibus; the Commune Sanctorum orations; and the temporal outside Holy Week. None of it is within a hundred lines of any post-1920 formulary listed above, and all of it is separately witnessed by the tracked venice-1570 and vatican-typica-1604 texts. What must NOT be quoted from these bytes on any basis this repository holds: the nine post-1920 formularies and the Praefatio de D. N. J. C. Rege, at the loci given in `rights_basis`.

OCR QUALITY. Measured by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin function-word share of 0.2166 over 375,148 tokens, English 0.0345, classified `prose-latin`, and the item's own page_number_confidence is 91 at 600 ppi. The pages are prose and the ordinary damage is still there: word-internal hyphenation at the narrow column measure is preserved as printed, so a search for a word broken across two lines fails; `dccrcta` for decreta at line 87 and `Prxfatio` for Praefatio at line 18849 are typical. ONE SYSTEMATIC LOSS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE SEARCHING. The Missal's internal page cross-references are gone: `ut infra in Canone 000` appears at lines 42536, 42730, 43601 and elsewhere, the printed folio number having been rendered as three zeroes throughout, so this text layer cannot be used to establish the book's own pagination or to follow a proper Communicantes to its page.

THE DROPPED INITIALS ARE A SEARCH HAZARD, AND ONE OF THEM HID THE DATE OF THE BOOK. Every large ornamental initial is emitted either as line noise or not at all, so `Te igitur` and `Quo primum` are both absent as strings while both texts are present in full. That much was already written on this record on 2026-08-01, as a warning, with those two examples. The next day the same defect was walked into while dating the printing: the Assumption Introit `Signum magnum` of 1950 is stored as `ignum magnum` at line 86903, so a literal search for it returns only the Apocalypse pericope at 68260 and a pro aliquibus locis Mass at 122030, and anyone reading that result as an absence dates the body seven years too early. Do not rest a negative search on this text layer: the raw-line modes establish absence of a string, not absence of a text.

WHAT THE TEXT LAYER CONTAINS AND WHERE. The approbation decree of 25 July 1920 stands at lines 7 to 64; the bull Quo primum follows, headed `PIUS EPISCOPUS / SERVUS SERVORUM DEI` at lines 70 to 74 and opening at line 77 with its ornamental Q dropped, `uo primum tempore ad`; the general rubrics and the Ritus servandus run from about line 9167; the Canon is present entire, headed `CANON` at line 49251 and opening at line 49260, again with the ornamental capital dropped, as `E IGITUR, / clementissi- / me Pater`; and the appendix of Masses `PRO ALIQUIBUS LOCIS` announced by the decree begins at line 113886. The file ends at line 123276 inside the Commune Sanctorum pro aliquibus locis, which is where the book ends and not where the scan was cut short.

IDENTITY. The item was uploaded on 2017-09-19 by a private uploader with an uploader-supplied title, `Missale Romanum (ed. Benedictus PP. XV, 1920)`, and no publisher, creator, date, or rights field. The scan's text layer opens on a running head and carries no title page, imprint, colophon, or copyright leaf anywhere. On 2026-08-01 that was recorded as an open gap -- the printing unestablished, the edition record naming the typical edition rather than the impression. On 2026-08-02 the gap closed in the direction nobody had drawn: the printing is not unknown so much as demonstrably late, 1970 or later on the appendix rubric and 1951-1954 in the body, and the edition record now says so. The date 1920 is the typical edition's own, established from the decree in the bytes, and was never a claim about the year this copy was struck.
artifacts.rights_basis: UNRESOLVED, AND THE REASON IS THAT THESE BYTES ARE NOT A 1920 PRINTING. This record stood `tracked` and `public-domain` from 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-02 on the ground of first publication before the pre-1931 United States line, `on that ground alone`. That ground was withdrawn on 2026-08-02 by the lane that owned this file, because the scanned book carries matter that was composed decades after 1931 and the pre-1931 line does not reach a page first published in 1944, or 1950, or 1955. WHAT WAS MEASURED, all of it re-verified in the hashed bytes on 2026-08-02 and every locus a physical line of the file named by `sha256` below. Nine post-1920 feasts stand in the book as full formularies with their ranks, not as marginal notes: S. Petri Canisii, canonized and declared Doctor 1925 (kalendarium 6195, formulary 72586); D. N. Jesu Christi Regis, instituted by Quas primas of 11 December 1925 (kalendarium 8133, formulary 94367 under `Dominica ultima Octobris`, `Duplex I classis`, with its own Praefatio indexed at 43750, 43801, 43888, 46553 and 46562 and its transfer and occurrence rubrics at 48595-48607); S. Joannis Mariae Vianney, canonized 1925 and universal 1928 (kalendarium 7284, formulary 86104); S. Joannis Eudes, canonized 1925 (kalendarium 7388, formulary 87420); S. Teresiae a Jesu Infante, canonized 1925 and extended to the universal calendar 1927 (kalendarium 7856, formulary 92091, `Die 3 Octobris ... Duplex`); S. Roberti Bellarmino, canonized 1930, Doctor 1931, feast 1932 (kalendarium 6378, formulary 74820); S. Joannis Bosco, canonized 1934 (kalendarium 5372, formulary 66667, `Die 31 Januarii ... Duplex`); Immaculati Cordis B. M. V., instituted 1944, at the 1944 grade in both places (kalendarium 7420 `duplex II classis`, formulary 87798 `In Festo / Immaculati Cordis B. M. V. / Duplex II classis`); and the Assumption printed with the Mass Signum magnum of 1950, whose Introit stands at 86903 as `ignum magnum apparuit in coelo` -- the dropped ornamental S is the initial this scan loses everywhere, and it is why a search for the string returns the wrong answer. THE DECISIVE ONE IS IN THE APPENDIX AND IT IS NOT A 1944-1954 BOOK. At appendix pages [223]-[224], running heads at lines 120199 and 120295, the Missae pro aliquibus locis carry a whole formulary `Eodem die 3 Septembris / S. Pii X. / Papae et Conf.` (heading 120221) for a pope canonized on 29 May 1954 and given a universal feast in 1955. Its rubric, at lines 120225-120228, reads: `Hoc Festum in Ecclesia universali ritu duplici celebratur, sed pro Fraternitate sacerdotali S. Pii X ritu duplici I classis cum Octava privilegiata III ordinis.` The Fraternitas sacerdotalis Sancti Pii X was erected on 1 November 1970. A rubric granting that body a proper rank and a privileged octave cannot have been composed before it existed, so the book these bytes were scanned from is a printing of 1970 or later, and in no case earlier than 1954. The appendix pagination runs through it unbroken -- [221] at 120048, [223] at 120199, [224] at 120298, [225] at 120394 -- so these are set pages in the sequence and not a slip laid in. WHAT BOUNDS THE BODY, AND WHY THE TWO BOUNDS DISAGREE. The body is a printing of 1951 to 1954: Signum magnum of 1950 is in it, the Assumption still has its common octave (kalendarium 7346, abolished 1955), and the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary of 1954, St Joseph the Worker of 1955, and St Pius X in the sanctoral proper for 3 September are all absent (`Opific` 0 hits, `Reginae` returning only the old pro aliquibus locis indults at 117131 and 117423, `Pii X` occurring at four lines and all four in the appendix). So the body is pre-1955 matter and the appendix is post-1970 matter, bound in one book. Whether the whole was reset for a modern reprint or leaves were substituted cannot be told from a text layer, and it does not matter to this record: the post-1954 matter is in the bytes either way. WHAT THE PRE-1931 GROUND STILL CARRIES, WHICH IS MOST OF THE BOOK AND NOT THIS ARTIFACT. The typical edition of Benedict XV was published in 1920 and is out of United States copyright; nothing here disturbs that, and see the edition record. Under 17 U.S.C. 103(b) the copyright in a later compilation `extends only to the material contributed by the author of such work` and `does not imply any exclusive right in the preexisting material`, so a 1970s printing of the 1920 Missal enlarges nothing in the Canon, the Ordo Missae, the Ritus servandus, the temporal, the Commons or the sanctoral as the typical edition had them. THAT PROPOSITION IS ABOUT THE TEXT AND NOT ABOUT THE FILE, AND CONFLATING THE TWO IS THE ERROR BEING CORRECTED. 103(b) states what a later copyright does not reach; it is not a permission to redistribute what that copyright does reach, and these 2,918,085 bytes contain both. `tracked` in this repository means the exact artifact is lawful to distribute from the repository (guidance/sources.md:375-386), and the exact artifact includes formularies first published in 1925, 1944, 1950 and 1955 abroad, which is squarely inside the URAA restoration analysed at src/sources/inventories/missale-romanum-1962-facsimile-rights-v1.toml `[the_underlying_edition.uraa_conditions]`, and leaves of a post-1970 foreign printing besides, which need no formality to be protected at all. So the file may not sit in Git and the question of who holds what in the added matter is open. `unresolved` means here what it means on the 1962 facsimile: not that nobody looked, but that somebody looked and found matter with no basis. NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the download succeeded, or that the item carries no rights field. guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds the first two insufficient, and the third was never a basis in either direction.

edition.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Decretum approbationis editionis typicae Vaticanae of 25 July 1920, subscribed by A. Card. Vico, Bishop of Porto and S. Rufina, Prefect, and Alexander Verde, Secretary, by mandate of Benedict XV, declaring this edition typical and ordering that all future editions be conformed to it
edition.notes: The typical edition of Benedict XV: the Missal reset to follow Pius X's reform of the Psalter and Breviary. Its own approbation decree, printed at the head of the scanned copy and transcribed in the text layer at lines 7 to 64, states exactly what it changed and what it did not -- the edition is drawn from the typical edition of 1900 (`ex altera typica anni 1900 deprompta`) and innovates only what followed from the recent liturgical prescriptions and from the additions and variations introduced into the typical Breviary approved by decree of 25 March 1914 under the bull Divino afflatu and the motu proprio Abhinc duos annos, together with an appendix of Masses proper to particular places. THIS RECORD NAMES THE TYPICAL EDITION, NOT THE PRINTING SCANNED, AND ON 2026-08-02 THE PRINTING WAS DATED. The one artifact held is a scan whose text layer carries no title page, imprint, or copyright leaf; a licensed publisher's edition conformed to this typical edition would reprint the same approbation decree, so the decree alone never established that these bytes are the Vatican Polyglot printing rather than an editio iuxta typicam. As first written this record left it there, an open gap. It is no longer open, and the answer is later than anyone had drawn: THE SCANNED COPY IS A PRINTING OF 1970 OR LATER. Its appendix carries a whole Mass of St Pius X, canonized 1954, at appendix pages [223]-[224] in the unbroken running sequence, whose rubric grants the Fraternitas sacerdotalis S. Pii X -- erected 1 November 1970 -- a rank of duplex I classis with a privileged octave of the third order. Its body is separately a printing of 1951 to 1954: the Assumption is the Mass Signum magnum of 1950 and still has its common octave, and the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary of 1954, St Joseph the Worker of 1955 and St Pius X in the sanctoral are all absent. The loci and the searches are on the artifact record. THE TEXT IS STILL THIS EDITION'S AND THE RIGHTS ARE NOT. Nine feasts instituted between 1925 and 1955 stand in the scan as full formularies with their ranks, so the scan is a witness to the 1920 typical edition PLUS thirty-five years of accretion, and the artifact accordingly stands `remote` and `unresolved` holding no bytes rather than `tracked` and `public-domain` on the pre-1931 line, which does not reach a page composed in 1944. The 1920 typical edition itself is untouched by any of that: published 1920, out of United States copyright, and under 17 U.S.C. 103(b) no later printing's copyright enlarges anything in it. The sibling edition.catholic-church.missale-romanum.unidentified-pre-1955-witness-ia-1947 is a conformed publisher's edition, a Benziger Brothers editio IV iuxta typicam Vaticanam, and the two must not be merged: that one is a New York printing of about 1942, this one is the typical edition it was conformed to. If a later lane acquires a printing that can be shown to be a 1920 impression, it lands under this record and supersedes the artifact held here. THIS IS THE LAST TYPICAL EDITION BEFORE THE 1955 SIMPLIFICATION AND THE 1960 CODE. Its rubrics are the pre-1955 ones -- the double, semidouble, and simple grades run throughout the scanned text layer, `semiduplex` alone appearing 169 times -- and its Holy Week is the pre-1955 one, the Ritus servandus directing the deacon through the prophecies of Holy Saturday from the first prophecy to the blessing. The appendix of Masses `PRO ALIQUIBUS LOCIS` that the approbation decree announces is in fact present in the scan, so the copy is a printing of the announced contents and not an abridgement of them -- but it is an ENLARGEMENT of them, and that is where its date was finally read. It is a witness to the state of the Roman Missal that the 1962 edition revised, not to the 1962 edition.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The Roman Rite altar book containing the Order of Mass, the temporal and sanctoral cycles, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, and related rubrical and ritual material. Edition records distinguish the authoritative typical edition from publisher-produced editions made according to it.
